decisions.reason: As an organic variant of a core ham product, it fits the firm's strategic expansion of organic lines and a large incumbent would usually retain such a close-to-business item unless sales clearly fell below aspiration.

This product is still close to the established cured-meat range and supports the organic portfolio, so boundedly rational management would likely continue it while monitoring whether demand reaches acceptable levels.

Organic pepper salami is a familiar extension of the firm's salami competence, and with organizational slack the firm would normally keep this relatively low-risk line unless performance proved persistently weak.

The teriyaki aspic beef specialty looks like a more experimental niche deli-counter item, so if its results lag aspirations the firm is likely to reallocate those resources back to stronger standard products or new projects.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is a narrower taste variant than the firm's mainstream offer, making it more likely to miss aspiration levels and be discontinued in a portfolio clean-up.

Liver pâté with veal remains close to the firm's premium pâté capability, and a large established producer would often keep such a line for another cycle unless internal sales evidence clearly justified exit.
